name: Economics
fw: C3 D2.Eco K–8 / IL SS.EC 9–12 / CEE
fwnote: Codes are C3 economics indicators (D2.Eco.x.band) and the 2021 National Standards for Personal Financial Education (named by area) for K–8, Illinois 9–12 economics and financial-literacy standards (SS.EC.x.9-12, SS.EC.FL.x.9-12), and CEE Voluntary National Content Standards in Economics, 2nd ed. 2010 (CEE 1–20); alignment was made by the course author and is not a certification by any of these bodies.

1.bq: How do people choose what they need and want?
std: D2.Eco.1.K-2
Explain how scarcity means people have to make choices.
D2.Eco.2.K-2
Identify the benefits and costs of personal decisions.
CEE 1
Productive resources are limited, so people must choose some things and give up others.
CEE 2
Good decisions compare the extra costs and extra benefits of a choice.

7.bq: How do people and whole societies decide what to do with things that are scarce?
std: Explain how economic decisions affect the well-being of people, businesses and society.
CEE 1
Productive resources are limited, so people must choose some things and give up others.
CEE 2
Good decisions compare the extra costs and extra benefits of a choice.
CEE 3
Societies use different methods, such as markets, command and tradition, to decide what to produce and for whom.
CEE 4
People respond in predictable ways to positive and negative incentives.
